topic: Q4 decode GEMV kernel efficiency on the M1: achieved bandwidth vs peak, and digest-preserving kernel-internal candidates (load scheduling, workgroup sizing)
outcome: receipt-only NEGATIVE: no candidate repeated a gain, so no source change, no test change, and no digest legs. The production kernel is unchanged at main 4b760947.
host: jwm1-linux, Apple M1 (G13G B1), Honeykrisp, linux-asahi 7.1.6, glslc 2026.3; dev box llvmpipe (LLVM 15.0.6 lvp) for the correctness screen

production_baseline.source: receipts/2026-09-09-decode-fusion/profile-cand and m1-raw per-size profiles, 32-token runs of pinned Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-4bit, quiet machine

bandwidth.traffic_note: weights 0.5 B/el + scale+bias 8 B per 64-el group = 0.625 B/el over 14,909,440 weight elements, plus x rows and outputs (~34 KB)
bandwidth.achieved_gb_s_production: 9.36 MB / 7.804 ms = 1.20 GB/s (best profile); 1.09-1.20 GB/s across the four profiles
bandwidth.headroom: ~57x nominal; the kernel chain runs at ~1.8% of LPDDR4X peak, so DRAM bandwidth is not the binding constraint at short context
bandwidth.floor_note: receipts/2026-09-09-decode-fusion/floor.json: ~28-30 us GPU floor per dispatch through the encoder; 96 x ~28 us = 2.7 ms of the 7.8 ms is floor. The non-floor remainder (~5.1 ms) still runs at only ~1.8 GB/s.

bench_isolated_kernel_ticks.note: raw dispatches, quiet machine, warm 9.3 MB working set (SLC-resident), device timestamp units at reported period 1.0 ns. Absolute ticks are unit-caveat: the same runs' 512 MB copy probe reads 49125 ticks = '10.9 TB/s', which is physical nonsense, so honeykrisp timestamp periods must not be trusted for absolute bandwidth; same-run ratios are valid. Production numbers above anchor the absolute scale.
bench_isolated_kernel_ticks.reading: A 144-workgroup dispatch costs ~16 us raw even when its 585 KB fit in cache; gate_up's 4.9 MB in ~34.6 us is ~1.1 us/100KB against a floor that is already half its runtime. Load-issue latency is not the limiter; the launch/drain floor and latency-boundedness are.

candidates.constraint: the lane->word map, fma pairing, and precise markers are pinned bit-for-bit to native qmv by receipts/2026-09-09-q4-gemv-order, so every candidate had to keep the exact per-lane word sequence and arithmetic order; only instruction scheduling and workgroup mapping could vary

unroll_paired_two_words.form: the plain qmv tile walks two words per iteration in the same lane order (w then w+LANES, general tail loop), letting the second half's weight/x loads issue while the first half's math is in flight
unroll_paired_two_words.llvmpipe_screen: bit-exact 7/7 outputs (tree variant); 4-18% slower on the software renderer (expected, not decision-bearing)

loadfirst_explicit.form: both words, both x quads, and all four scale/bias values of a pair iteration load before any math (six outstanding loads)
loadfirst_explicit.verdict: flat on three shapes and REGRESSES the o shape by 68-81% in both legs (a real, repeated pathology, not noise); rejected outright

wg128_four_columns.form: local_size_x 256->128, COLUMNS_PER_GROUP 8->4, grid doubles; pure scheduling-granularity change, no arithmetic change (subgroup path has no workgroup barriers)
wg128_four_columns.verdict: flat within noise; no repeatable gain. Note: production adoption would also require a new kernel id and a primitives.cpp dispatch change, so the bar was 'clear repeatable win'; it did not clear it

rejected_without_measurement.wider_word_loads: a lane's next word is w+32 (LANES stride), so a uvec2 load would change which words a lane owns - that changes the reduction's rounding and the digests; forbidden by the order receipt
rejected_without_measurement.scale_bias_hoisting: each lane's words land in distinct groups (stride 32 words = 4 groups), so per-lane scale/bias loads are already once per group; the 8x cross-lane reuse is same-address and cache-served
rejected_without_measurement.qmv_fast_tile: requires k % 512 == 0; the model's k values are 896 and 4864, both ≡ 384 mod 512, so native Metal itself uses the plain tile on this model
rejected_without_measurement.x_staging_in_shared_memory: needs a workgroup barrier on a path that dropped barriers to win; the x row is ~2-10 KB and cache-resident

correctness_instrument.what: tools/q4-bw-bench (branch q4-gemv-bandwidth, commit fa4fe987 + bench refactor): compiles the frozen production shader (sha256 7e57b15d..., byte-identical to overlay/mlx/backend/omarchy/shaders/qmm_vec.comp at 4b760947, asserted by run-m1.sh diff gate) and each candidate from identical input buffers on the exact four per-layer dispatch shapes with the production push-constant/binding contract of dispatch_quantized_gemv_group
correctness_instrument.bit_exactness: 0 bit mismatches in every compare: 4 M1 legs (subgroup path, subgroupSize 32 + ARITHMETIC) x 21 compares (3 sides x 7 dim outputs) and llvmpipe tree-path screens
correctness_instrument.digest_gate_status: not exercised: no source change is being landed, so the six canonical Q4 digests (short 7fd25a869ff21678, long 4cc08910089477fd, longctx 7da83f06ec9f001d, on both sides of any pair) have nothing new to gate; any future candidate from this file must gate them on a quiet machine with retry-on-mismatch (contention flips qmm dispatches to the tile fallback, which is NOT digest-neutral - see receipts/2026-09-10-qmm-splitk-parity/verdict.json)

conclusion: The Q4 decode kernel has no repeatable digest-preserving kernel-internal gain left at short context: load scheduling and workgroup mapping are measured flat (one variant regresses), and the binding constraints are the per-dispatch launch/drain floor plus encoder/driver overhead, which are outside this assignment. Achieved bandwidth is ~1.1-1.2 GB/s against a 68 GB/s part, quantifying the headroom that dispatch-count and driver-side work (already-owned levers) would have to reclaim.
artifacts: tools/q4-bw-bench/shaders/ (base frozen copy + unroll + loadfirst + wg128 + peak probes)
